scenario.name: CircleCI Official Security Alert, GitHub Security & CISA — CircleCI CI/CD Supply Chain Breach: Engineer macOS Infostealer, 2FA Session Theft & Customer Vault Exfiltration
scenario.overview: Picture an international border crossing checkpoint with glass passport inspection booths, zig-zag queue stanchions, an X-ray luggage conveyor belt, and a striped crossing barrier. Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station. A secondary customs officer cross-checks the border passport registry and catches a stamp serial number that was never issued by that embassy. In this scenario (T1539, CircleCI Official Security Alert, GitHub Security & CISA, CircleCI CI/CD Supply Chain Breach: Engineer macOS Infostealer, 2FA Session Theft & Customer Vault Exfiltration), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: engineer macOS Infostealer Infection, then session Replay from Foreign IP, Production, then offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Engineer macOS Infostealer Infection, then Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production, then Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets. Primary detection pivots on EDR Event 1 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production Database Access & KMS Key Extraction
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Collection (T1550.004 - Web Session Cookie / T1552)
stages.description: While the customs scanner checks only the outer cover of the passport, the forged interior page clears the glass booth and the striped crossing barrier swings upward. Here in Step 2 inside the border control, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station without disturbing the diplomatic sealed pouch lane. Replaying the stolen engineer session token from a remote proxy IP, the attacker accesses privileged internal CircleCI production hosts, extracts database encryption keys from the running runtime environment, and dumps customer project databases containing encrypted environment variables and OAuth tokens (logged in CloudTrail Event 200 with SessionAnomaly=SSO session cookie replayed from new ASN/IP, CompromisedAssets=Production Datastores + Runtime Encryption Keys so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS runtime decryption keys (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.004 during "Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production Database Access & KMS Key Extraction" , Replaying the stolen engineer session token from a remote proxy IP, the attacker accesses privileged internal CircleCI production hosts, extracts database encryption keys from the running runtime environment, and dumps customer project databases containing encrypted environment variables and OAuth tokens while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ aws-kms / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Engineer macOS Laptop (Infostealer Malware)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer CI/CD Secrets, SSH Keys & GitHub Tokens).

keySpecs.value: Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS runtime decryption keys
Require step-up hardware FIDO2 re-authentication for every production bastion login or KMS decryption key access regardless of active SSO cookie state.

stages.title: Stage 3: Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement & Impact (T1552.001 - Credentials In Files / T1199 - Trusted Relationship)
stages.description: Rolling luggage smoothly off the X-ray conveyor into the secure arrival hall, the traveler crosses the border wearing an official-looking entry clearance. In this final step inside the border control, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station until the customs passport registry catches the mismatch. Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens) offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts (logged in CloudTrail Event 1 with ExfiltratedSecrets=Customer Environment Variables, SSH Deploy Keys, GitHub OAuth Tokens, ArchitecturalDefense=Short-lived OIDC Federated Tokens instead of static CI secrets so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Offline AES-GCM Decryption of Customer Project Contexts -> Recover AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH Private Keys (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Offline AES-GCM Decryption of Customer Project Contexts -> Recover AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay" , Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ github-audit / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Engineer macOS Laptop (Infostealer Malware)) to Node ④ (#4 CircleCI Production Bastion & KMS Key Service), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer CI/CD Secrets, SSH Keys & GitHub Tokens).

steps.storyAnalogy: Rolling luggage smoothly off the X-ray conveyor into the secure arrival hall, the traveler crosses the border wearing an official-looking entry clearance.
